question: The Commission recently launched an online survey addressed directly to farmers on how to simplify the CAP for farmers and national administrations.

Beyond this necessary gathering of evidence, the Commission also says it is proposing short- and medium-term measures that could bring some relief to farmers, but also to national administrations which represent the first point of contact for farmers and are responsible for managing and paying EU funds. However, in Ireland, implementation and administration are poor and under-resourced.
Delays of payments by the Irish national administration and other questionable issues have occurred. 1.
How does the Commission plan to use the feedback from Irish farmers to address specific national concerns and obstacles, and what timeline can it provide?

Moreover, what mechanisms will be put in place to ensure that the simplification measures are effectively implemented at the national level in Ireland, providing tangible relief for farmers, including from administrative and bureaucratic burdens and duplication?
Is the Commission exploring the possibility of additional targeted revisions or a total revision of the CAP in the next mandate?
answer: The first insights of the survey ‘Simplification — the farmers point of view’ were published on 12 April 2024 (1). Further analysis of the replies will follow. In addition, in-depth interviews with selected respondents will be conducted to understand the background and rationale behind the replies they provided.

This will feed a dedicated study on simplification and administrative burden for farmers to be published by end of 2024. The Commission will share the outcome of this project with Member States and stakeholders also to facilitate national level improvements, where applicable.

The Commission has organised exchanges with Member States in expert group setting, in the common agricultural policy (CAP) network forum as well as in bilateral meetings to discuss simplification proposals, to encourage exchanges of best practice and to guide Member States and other stakeholders in take-up of simplification actions.

Assistance will also be provided during the amendment process of the CAP Strategic Plans following the recent modification of the CAP legislation (2). Lessons learned in the ongoing simplification process will also feed the reflection on possible changes to the CAP after 2027.
